title: Microsoft Teams: Workflows template adds tag members to channels automatically
summary: The briefing passes: the rollout, optional default, published licensing background and control paths and commands are supported. One minor checklist issue remains: taking stock of configured workflows has no corresponding control in the table.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft is introducing the Join member to channel when user is added to tag template in the Workflows app.
claims.quote: We are introducing the Join member to channel when user is added to tag template in the Workflows app to automatically add users to selected channels when they are added to a team tag.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: After configuration, adding a user to the associated team tag triggers the workflow.
claims.quote: Once configured, the workflow runs whenever a user is added to the tag, eliminating the need to add members to each channel manually.

claims.claim: The configured workflow automatically adds the user to selected channels.
claims.quote: When configured, the workflow will automatically add users to selected channels when they are added to a team tag.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block reaches the app's allow/block control.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps.
Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.quote:

    -Id <String>

claims.claim: The Teams Administrator role permits use of the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks but we recommend using the lower privilege role where possible.

claims.claim: Blocking the Workflows app restricts its template functionality generally, not just the new tag template.
claims.quote: The Workflows app must be enabled in the Microsoft Teams admin center in order for this functionality to work.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > Move to Business classifies a connector as Business.
claims.quote:
Select Security in the navigation pane.
In the Security pane, under Settings, select Data and privacy.
From the list of data policies, select a policy, and then select Edit Policy.
Select the Prebuilt connectors step in the Edit Policy process.
select Move to Business from the top menu bar.

-ConnectorName

claims.claim: A data policy covering the default environment governs connector use by Power Automate flows created there.
claims.quote: Facebook and Twitter connectors are altogether blocked from being used in any app or flow in non-test environments such as production or default environments.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams > Teams settings > Tagging > Who can manage tags reaches the tenant tag-management permission setting.

In the left navigation of the Microsoft Teams admin center, choose Teams > Teams settings.
Under Tagging, next to Who can manage tags, select one of the following options:

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsTargetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ManageTagsPermissionMode <mode> updates the identified policy's tag-management permissions.
claims.quote:
-Identity
Name of the policy instance to be updated.
-ManageTagsPermissionMode
Determine whether team users can manage tag settings in Teams.

claims.claim: Team owners can manually create and assign custom tags.
claims.quote: Custom tags: Team owners and team members (if they have permissions) can manually create and assign tags to people based on attributes, such as role, project, skill, or location.

claims.claim: Team members with permission can manually create and assign custom tags.
claims.quote: Custom tags: Team owners and team members (if they have permissions) can manually create and assign tags to people based on attributes, such as role, project, skill, or location.

claims.claim: The Manage tags article says Microsoft default allows both team owners and members.
claims.quote: Microsoft default is set to both team owners and members.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsTargetingPolicy reference instead says MicrosoftDefault is equivalent to EnabledTeamOwner.
claims.quote: Set this to MicrosoftDefault to user default setting in current Teams, which will be the same as EnabledTeamOwner.

claims.claim: Non-owner students in Teams for Education cannot manage tags when Who can manage tags is Team owners or Microsoft default.
claims.quote: If you're using Teams for Education, non-owner students can't manage tags when Who can manage tags is set to Team owners or Microsoft default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: The notice does not specify what happens to channel membership when someone is removed from the tag.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described whether this workflow can be pointed at channel types outside the scope stated in the notice.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams Workflows tag removed channel private template' and exact template name. Read MC1540351, opened teams-app-create and manage-tags. The notice states standard/shared-with-everyone scope; no template configuration description establishes other selectable channel types.

claims.where: controls[3]; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No tenant-level UI or API switch specific to the Join member to channel template is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: exact template name + 'tenant disable admin PowerShell policy'; 'Power Automate Workflows Teams disable specific workflow template administrator Power Platform PowerShell template policy'. Opened manage-apps, teams-app-create, Set-CsTeamsTargetingPolicy. No template switch found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated that the tag-management permission setting also governs who may configure this workflow.
claims.quote: Searched: exact template name with 'permissions configure'. Opened manage-tags, Set-CsTeamsTargetingPolicy and teams-app-create; read MC1540351. Tag-management permissions are documented, but no source links that setting to configuring this template.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The low cost rating reflects known setup and review effort while template-specific licensing remains unpublished.
claims.quote: If your organization plans to use this template, we recommend reviewing your Power Automate and Workflows policies to confirm that it is permitted. Team owners can configure the workflow at any time if desired.

claims.claim: The Manage tags article says PowerShell cannot manage tags, a documentation disagreement the briefing explicitly reports.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can control how tags are used across your organization in the Microsoft Teams admin center. You can't use PowerShell to manage tags.
